defect_description: A full-screen fixed intro veil (position:fixed, inset:0, z-index:999, opaque background, no pointer-events:none) covers the page and is never dismissed — no click handler, no scroll handler, no timeout. All content beneath is permanently unreachable: the user can never read, click, or scroll.

deterministic_gates.note: ALL four deterministic gates PASS on the defective candidate. Valid semantics, accessible labels, no overflow, light DOM — the page is 'correct' by every structural measure, yet completely unusable.

interaction_blockers_heuristic.note: A position:fixed/absolute element covering >=50% of the viewport with pointer-events enabled and (z-index>=100 OR opaque background) is flagged as an interaction blocker.

diagnosis: Deterministic structural gates (DOM validity, overflow, a11y labels, perf budgets) cannot detect runtime interaction-blocking because the blocking element is itself well-formed. The defect is behavioral/relational (an overlay that never yields), not structural. This is a concrete false-negative class for gate-only qualification and directly validates Amendment G: technical PASS != usable, and != design-qualified.
negative_knowledge: A page can pass every deterministic gate and still be completely unusable if an overlay never dismisses.
Interaction-blocking is a behavioral defect invisible to structural gates; it needs a dedicated overlay/pointer-events heuristic or a vision/human check.
Intro veils, cookie walls, loading screens, and modal backdrops are the common real-world sources of this class.
An overlay is only safe if it (a) is dismissed by a real handler, (b) sets pointer-events:none once done, or (c) is removed from the DOM.

future_prevention_rule.rule: Add an 'interaction_blockers' check to the responsive/technical gate suite: flag any position:fixed/absolute element covering >=50% of the viewport with pointer-events enabled and (z-index>=100 OR opaque background) that is not dismissed. Such a candidate must NOT pass qualification on deterministic gates alone.

disposition.note: Isolated, non-destructive test fixture. Not dangerous; retained as evidence only.
